Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

these are field notes from the north side of Bellwether Ridge, mostly from the August 18–20 traverse, with a few observations added later in the same notebook. the cover says “M. Later the same morning, the notebook records a stop at the first bend of Alder Creek. The water was clear at the edge but clouded where it crossed a patch of fine sediment. The arrow is part of the page, but there's no need to explain what it means.

page 18 has an account of talking with a local trail guide at the north fork. The guide is reported as saying, “the creek only runs after a hard rain.” Keep that quotation as a quotation and keep it attached to the north-fork entry; don't present it as something Mara measured or confirmed. The next lines say there was no flow visible at the crossing on August 19, at 11:40 a.m. Those two things can sit next to each other in the transcription without trying to reconcile them. A little farther down is “old cut? maybe quarry,” including the question mark. Keep the uncertainty in that note rather than making it a definite quarry identification.

there are more useful details on pages 19–22. Page 19 records a tan layer over a fractured gray unit at marker B-6, then a note that the contact disappears beneath talus to the south. On page 20, the entry at 2:25 p.m. describes a rounded quartz pebble in the dry channel, about 3 cm long, and says it was left in place. Keep “left in place”; don't say it was collected. Page 21 has a small list of three sample bag labels, B6-1, B6-2 and C1-1, and next to them the words “labels checked at camp.” Preserve the hyphens and the labels in that order. Page 22 has a note that the afternoon light made the west-facing wall difficult to photograph, followed by “try before noon next time.” This is a notebook note, not a request for you to plan a trip.

pages 23 through 25 continue the August 20 route along the lower rim. Page 23 gives a time of 8:05 a.m. and a location written “below split pinnacle”; preserve that wording, even if it sounds informal. The entry describes a narrow seam with a rusty surface and says the seam pinches out about two paces east. On page 24 there is a rough scale written “1:25?”; keep the question mark and don't silently correct or remove it. Page 25 includes a short note about wind lifting loose paper from the map board, and a separate line saying the barometer was unreadable because its glass was fogged. Don't convert the barometer note into a pressure value. There are also small pencil ticks beside two lines; include readable words beside them, but don't invent labels for the ticks.

page 26 is a later comparison note, dated Aug. 23, and page 27 is a page of location reminders. Keep those after the traverse entries because that's their order in the notebook, even though the comparison is dated later. The comparison says “same pale band?” and mentions a photograph numbered 08-20-4; retain both the question mark and the full photo number. The reminders include “return for scale at B-6” and “ask N. about north fork name.” Preserve the initials as initials, and don't expand them or decide who N. is. Some pages have uppercase lettering and others are mostly lowercase; follow what is actually legible instead of regularizing everything to one style.

please don't supply a summary of the geology, identify formations, resolve uncertain wording, or add facts from outside the notebook. For the transcription, retain recognizable abbreviations, dates, units, symbols, and the distinction between an observation and a question or later reminder. If a word is genuinely unreadable, mark only that word or region as unclear in the transcription; don't guess it. But if the scans fail the condition above, use the fallback instead: no partial transcription, just a concise page-by-page account of what needs rescanning and a request for clearer scans.
